newsitem.title: NORWAY: Pension fund backs Storebrand-Christiania merger.
newsitem.headline: Pension fund backs Storebrand-Christiania merger.

text.p: Folketrygdfondet, the Norwegian state pension fund, said on Wednesday it backed the proposed merger between Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA and insurer Storebrand ASA.
The board of Folketrygdfondet voted unanimously in favour of the merger plan, chairman Henrik Lisaeth told Reuters.
Folketrygdfondet is one of the biggest shareholders in Storebrand, controlling about 10 percent of stock in the country's largest insurance company.
Both Christiania, Norway's second biggest bank, and Storebrand will hold extraordinary general meetings on June 26 to discuss the merger proposal.
Christiania and Storebrand announced plans in April to merge by the end of 1997 provided they win approval by shareholders and the Finance Ministry, the regulatory body.
